subject: pe
topicName: Short and Long Term Effects of Exercise

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The effects of exercise are categorised by how quickly they occur and how long they last: Immediate effects - occur during and straight after a single exercise session Short-term effects - occur up to 24-36 hours after exercise Long-term effects - occur after weeks and months of regular training (adaptations)

steps.title: Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS)
steps.body: Muscle pain and stiffness that develops 24-72 hours after exercise, particularly following eccentric muscle contractions or unaccustomed activity. Caused by microscopic tears (micro-tears) in muscle fibres, not by lactic acid build-up.

steps.title: Cardiac Hypertrophy
steps.body: The heart muscle (particularly the left ventricle) grows larger and stronger as a result of regular aerobic training. This allows the heart to pump more blood per beat.

steps.title: Bradycardia
steps.body: Resting heart rate decreases below 60 bpm in trained athletes. A larger, stronger heart can pump the same cardiac output with fewer beats because stroke volume has increased.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: State three immediate effects of exercise on the cardiovascular system. | What is DOMS and what causes it? | Explain the difference between cardiac hypertrophy and bradycardia.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always categorise effects as immediate, short-term or long-term - examiners check this DOMS is caused by micro-tears, NOT lactic acid - this is a very common trick question Link cardiac hypertrophy and bradycardia - one causes the other Use precise terminology: "capillarisation" not "more blood vessels" When asked about long-term effects, link each adaptation to its sporting benefit Know the difference between hypertrophy (muscle growth) and hyperplasia (increase in cell number) - GCSE focuses on hypertrophy
